''[[A Very Long Engagement]]'' }} '''Jean-Pierre Jeunet''' ({{IPA|fr|ʒɑ̃ pjɛʁ ʒœnɛ|lang}}; born 3 September 1953) is a French director and screenwriter. Jeunet debuted as a director with the 1991 black comedy ''[[Delicatessen (1991 film)|Delicatessen]],'' collaborating with [[Marc Caro]]. Jeunet then co-wrote and -directed with Caro again on ''[[The City of Lost Children]]'' (1995). His work with science fiction and horror led him to direct ''[[Alien Resurrection]]'' (1997), the fourth film in the [[Alien (franchise)|''Alien'' film series]] and his first and thus far only American film. In 2001, Jeunet achieved his biggest success with ''[[Amélie]]'', which won him international acclaim; the film reached [[BBC's 100 Greatest Films of the 21st Century]].Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211211/388cuJ-dR4I Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20180927064934/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=388cuJ-dR4I Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite video|publisher=[[YouTube]]|title=Jean-Pierre Jeunet: A Life In Pictures|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=388cuJ-dR4I}}{{cbignore}} ==Life and career== Jean-Pierre Jeunet was born in [[Roanne]], France.{{cite book|title=501 Movie Directors|editor-first=Steven Jay|editor-last=Schneider|publisher=Cassell Illustrated|location=London|year=2007|page=549|isbn=9781844035731|oclc=1347156402}} He bought his first camera at the age of 17 and made short films while studying animation at Cinémation Studios. He befriended [[Marc Caro]], a designer and comic book artist who became his longtime collaborator and co-director. They met at an animation festival in Annecy in the 1970s.{{Cite book|title=Jean-Pierre Jeunet|last=Ezra|first=Elizabeth|publisher=Library of Congress Cataloging-in-Publication Data|year=2008|location=Chicago}} Together, Jeunet and Caro directed award-winning animations. Their first live-action film was ''The Bunker of the Last Gunshots'' (1981), a short film about soldiers in a bleak futuristic world. Jeunet also directed numerous advertisements and music videos, such as [[Jean-Michel Jarre]]'s ''[[Zoolook]]'' (together with Caro).{{citation needed|date=October 2018}} Jeunet's films often resonate with the late twentieth-century French film movement ''[[cinéma du look]]'' and allude to themes and aesthetics involving [[German expressionist cinema|German expressionism]], French [[poetic realism]], and the [[French New Wave]]. Jeunet and Caro's first feature film was ''[[Delicatessen (1991 film)|Delicatessen]]'' (1991), a melancholy [[black comedy|comedy]] set in a [[famine]]-plagued post-apocalyptic world, in which an apartment building above a delicatessen is ruled by a butcher who kills people in order to feed his tenants.{{cite web|work=[[The New York Times]]|url=https://www.nytimes.com/movie/review?res=9D0CEEDF1538F936A35753C1A967958260|title=Review/Film Festival; Please, How Many Lentils for Your Musical Saw?|author-link=Janet Maslin|author=Maslin, Janet|date=5 October 1991}} They next made ''[[The City of Lost Children]]'' (1995), a dark, multi-layered [[fantasy film]] about a mad scientist who steals children's dreams so that he can live indefinitely.{{cite web|title=FILM REVIEW;Out of the Fever Dreams of a Child|author-link=Stephen Holden|author=Holden, Stephen|date=15 December 1995|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131007230141/https://movies.nytimes.com/movie/review?res=9B02E0DD1739F936A25751C1A963958260|url-status=live|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1995/12/15/movies/film-review-out-of-the-fever-dreams-of-a-child.html|archive-date=2013-10-07|url-access=subscription|work=[[The New York Times]]}} The success of ''The City of Lost Children'' led to an invitation to direct the fourth film in the ''[[Alien (franchise)|Alien]]'' series, ''[[Alien Resurrection]]'' (1997).{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1997/11/26/movies/film-review-ripley-believe-it-or-not-has-a-secret-and-it-s-not-pretty.html|work=[[The New York Times]]|title=FILM REVIEW; Ripley, Believe It or Not, Has a Secret, and It's Not Pretty|author=Maslin, Janet|author-link=Janet Maslin|archive-date=2015-05-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150527070850/https://www.nytimes.com/1997/11/26/movies/film-review-ripley-believe-it-or-not-has-a-secret-and-it-s-not-pretty.html|url-access=subscription|url-status=live|date=26 November 1997}} This is where Jeunet and Caro ended up going their separate ways, as Jeunet believed this to be an amazing opportunity whereas Caro was not interested in working on a big-budget Hollywood movie on which he would lack creative control. Caro ended up assisting for a few weeks with costumes and set design, but then he decided to start a solo career in illustration and computer graphics. Jeunet directed ''[[Amélie]]'' (2001), the story of a woman who takes pleasure in doing good deeds but has trouble finding love herself, which starred [[Audrey Tautou]].{{cite web|title=Film; Going Sweet and Sentimental Has Its Rewards|first=Daniel|last=Zalewski|date=28 October 2001|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2001/10/28/movies/film-going-sweet-and-sentimental-has-its-rewards.html|work=[[The New York Times]]}} ''Amélie'' was a huge critical and commercial success worldwide and was nominated for several [[Academy Awards]]. For his work on the film, Jeunet won a [[European Film Awards|European Film Award]] for Best Director.{{cite web |title=European Film Awards, 2001, The Winners |url=https://members.europeanfilmacademy.org/European-Film-Awards-Winners-2001.72.0.html |website=European Film Academy |access-date=23 January 2023}} In 2004, Jeunet released ''[[A Very Long Engagement]]'', an adaptation of the novel by [[Sébastien Japrisot]]. The film, starring Audrey Tautou and [[Jodie Foster]], chronicled a woman's search for her missing lover after [[World War I]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/11/26/movies/26enga.html|work=[[The New York Times]]|title=A Love That Won't Surrender to War, Death and Oblivion|author-link=Manohla Dargis|author=Dargis, Manohla|date=26 November 2004}} In 2005 Jean-Pierre Jeunet was involved in the creation of a detailed history project about the life of French aviator [[Louis Blériot]]. After a year Jeunet felt the movie was too close in historic timeline to ''A Very Long Engagement'' and the project was abandoned.{{citation |url=https://archive.org/details/ASG-Bleriot-2025|title=Lit 18: "Blériot!" (2025)|publisher=Internet Archive|date=11 February 2025|access-date=12 February 2025}} In 2009, he released ''[[Micmacs (film)|Micmacs]]'',{{cite web|title=An Eye for Detail, an Imagination at Play|first=Mekado|last=Murphy|date=21 May 2010|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/05/23/movies/23micmacs.html|work=[[The New York Times]]}} which is about a man and his friends who come up with an intricate and original plan to destroy two big weapons manufacturers.{{Citation|last=Jeunet|first=Jean-Pierre|title=Micmacs|date=2010-06-11|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1149361/|access-date=2016-07-01}} Jeunet has also directed numerous commercials, including a 2'25" film for [[Chanel N° 5]] featuring his frequent collaborator Audrey Tautou.{{Citation|last=Foiret|first=Cyril|title=Audrey Tatou for Chanel No. 5 Commercial|date=2009-04-05|url=https://trendland.com/audrey-tautou-for-chanel-n5-commercial/|access-date=2026-11-11}} In 2013, Jeunet released ''[[The Young and Prodigious T. S. Spivet]]'', an adaptation of [[Reif Larsen]]'s book ''[[The Selected Works of T.S. Spivet]]'' that starred Kyle Catlett.{{Cite web|url=https://variety.com/2013/film/reviews/film-review-the-young-and-prodigious-t-s-spivet-1200677021/|title=Film Review: 'The Young and Prodigious T.S. Spivet'|last=Weissberg|first=Jay|date=2013-09-28|website=Variety|language=en|access-date=2019-04-21}} In 2016, Jeunet and Romain Segaud co-directed the three-minute stop-motion animation film ''Deux escargots s'en vont'', based on a poem by [[Jacques Prévert]]. Since his last release, Jeunet has tried to get other projects funded but has found it impossible to find investors willing to take a risk on his quirky films. He stated in 2019 that he may go to Netflix "as a last resort",{{cite news |last1=Aguilar |first1=Carlos |title=Jean-Pierre Jeunet Is Making an 'Amelie' Mockumentary and a Sci-Fi Animated Feature — Exclusive |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2019/05/jean-pierre-jeunet-amelie-mockumentary-1202131545/#! |access-date=14 December 2019 |work=IndieWire |publisher=Penske Business Media, LLC. |date=6 May 2019}} and indeed his next film, ''[[Bigbug]]'', was released by the streaming video company in 2022. ==Filmography== === Feature film === {| class="wikitable" |- !
